component.name: kudu
component.title: Kudu
component.description: Insert, update, upsert, delete and scan rows of Apache Kudu tables, and create tables.
component.label: database,iot,cloud

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

kuduClient.label: advanced
kuduClient.description: To use a custom org.apache.kudu.client.KuduClient for all the endpoints of this component. When it is set or autowired, the endpoints do not create a client for the host and port of their URI, and do not shut the client down when they stop.

CamelKuduSchema.description: The org.apache.kudu.Schema with the columns of the table that the CREATE_TABLE operation creates. Required for CREATE_TABLE.

CamelKuduTableOptions.description: The options of the table that the CREATE_TABLE operation creates, such as its partitioning and its number of replicas. Required for CREATE_TABLE, and the options must set range or hash partitioning.

CamelKuduScanColumnNames.description: The names of the columns that the SCAN operation returns for each row. If not set, the scan returns all the columns of the table.

CamelKuduScanPredicate.description: The predicate on a column that the rows of the SCAN operation must match. If not set, the scan returns all the rows of the table.

CamelKuduScanLimit.description: The maximum number of rows that the SCAN operation returns. The value must be a java.lang.Long, as an Integer or a String fails the exchange. If not set, the number of rows is not limited.

producerIn.description: For insert, update, upsert and delete: a Map of the column names and their values, one row, each value of the Java type of its column (a String for an INT32 column fails); delete uses only the key columns. Text such as JSON, a List or a POJO fails: unmarshal it into a Map first. Scan and create_table do not read the body: they take the CamelKuduScan* and the CamelKuduSchema and CamelKuduTableOptions headers. The operation must be set

producerOut.description: Scan gives a List of the rows, each a Map of the column names and their values, an empty List for no rows. The other operations leave the body unchanged

host.label: common
host.description: The host name or IP address of the Kudu master. The endpoint creates its Kudu client for this host and port, unless the kuduClient component option is set.

port.label: common
port.description: The RPC port of the Kudu master, which is 7051 in a default Kudu installation.

tableName.label: common
tableName.description: The name of the Kudu table that the operation reads, writes or creates.

operation.description: The operation that the producer performs on the table. INSERT, UPDATE, UPSERT and DELETE write the one row in the Map of the message body, CREATE_TABLE creates the table from the CamelKuduSchema and CamelKuduTableOptions headers, and SCAN puts the rows of the table in the message body. There is no default, and an exchange fails when the option is not set.
